title: Representing lifts identify the right mate under arbitrary forgetting
statement:
Let $\mathcal W_X,\mathcal W_Y,\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ be locally small categories and let $U_X:\mathcal W_X\to\mathcal C_X$, $U_Y:\mathcal W_Y\to\mathcal C_Y$ be functors. Suppose $F^{\mathrm W}:\mathcal W_X\to\mathcal W_Y$ has a specified right adjoint $G^{\mathrm W}$ with unit $\eta^{\mathrm W}$ and counit $\epsilon^{\mathrm W}$, and $F:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ has a specified right adjoint $G$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$. Adjunction means natural mutually inverse Hom bijections, with transpose $u:K\to GL$ sent to $\epsilon_LF(u)$ and inverse $t\mapsto G(t)\eta_K$. Let $c:U_YF^{\mathrm W}\xrightarrow{\sim}FU_X$ be a natural isomorphism.

Suppose for each $L\in\mathcal W_Y$ there are an object $H_L\in\mathcal W_X$, an isomorphism $e_L:U_XH_L\xrightarrow{\sim}GU_YL$, and a morphism $d_L:F^{\mathrm W}H_L\to L$ such that $U_Y(d_L)=\epsilon_{U_YL}F(e_L)c_{H_L}$, and $u\mapsto d_LF^{\mathrm W}(u)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(K,H_L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F^{\mathrm W}K,L)$ for every $K$, naturally in $K$.

There is a unique isomorphism $h_L:G^{\mathrm W}L\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L$ with $d_LF^{\mathrm W}(h_L)=\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L$. The natural transformation $\beta:U_XG^{\mathrm W}\to GU_Y$, whose component is the ordinary adjunct of $U_Y(\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L)c_{G^{\mathrm W}L}^{-1}$, satisfies $\beta_L=e_LU_X(h_L)$ and is therefore a natural isomorphism. It is independent of all choices of representing triples and identifies both counits and units:
$$\epsilon_{U_YL}F(\beta_L)c_{G^{\mathrm W}L}=U_Y(\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L),\qquad G(c_K)\beta_{F^{\mathrm W}K}U_X(\eta^{\mathrm W}_K)=\eta_{U_XK}.$$
Here the right-mate transformation is the one defined in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] from $c^{-1}$ and the two specified adjunctions. No faithfulness or fullness of $U_X,U_Y$, and no functorial choice of representing triples, is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $L$ and abbreviate $A=G^{\mathrm W}L$, $H=H_L$, $d=d_L$. Write $P_K(v)=\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_LF^{\mathrm W}(v)$ and $Q_K(u)=dF^{\mathrm W}(u)$ for the two given bijections onto $\operatorname{Hom}(F^{\mathrm W}K,L)$. Define $h=Q_A^{-1}(\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L)$ and $k=P_H^{-1}(d)$. Functoriality gives $Q_H(hk)=\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_LF^{\mathrm W}(k)=d=Q_H(1_H)$ and $P_A(kh)=dF^{\mathrm W}(h)=\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L=P_A(1_A)$. Injectivity gives $hk=1_H$ and $kh=1_A$. Thus $h=h_L$ is an isomorphism; $Q_A$-injectivity also gives uniqueness among all morphisms satisfying the required counit equation.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with $L_1=F^{\mathrm W}$, $R_1=G^{\mathrm W}$, $L_2=F$, $R_2=G$, and its horizontal functors equal to $U_X,U_Y$; take $\alpha=c^{-1}:FU_X\to U_YF^{\mathrm W}$. It supplies a natural transformation $\beta:U_XG^{\mathrm W}\to GU_Y$. At $L$, its transpose is exactly $t_L=U_Y(\epsilon^{\mathrm W}_L)c_{G^{\mathrm W}L}^{-1}$, and therefore $\beta_L=G(t_L)\eta_{U_XG^{\mathrm W}L}$. This construction involves only the specified adjunctions and $c$.

proof.text:
Keep $L,A,H,h$ as in Step 1. Naturality of $c$ at $h:A\to H$ says $c_HU_Y(F^{\mathrm W}(h))=F(U_X(h))c_A$. Using the assumed equation for $U_Y(d)$ and the defining equation for $h$, compute
$$\epsilon_{U_YL}F(e_LU_X(h))=\epsilon_{U_YL}F(e_L)c_HU_Y(F^{\mathrm W}(h))c_A^{-1}=U_Y(dF^{\mathrm W}(h))c_A^{-1}=t_L.$$
The ordinary Hom bijection is injective, so this transpose computation gives $\beta_L=e_LU_X(h_L)$.

proof.text: Every component $\beta_L$ has inverse $q_L=U_X(h_L^{-1})e_L^{-1}$, as the two composites cancel using functoriality. These inverses are natural: for $a:L\to L'$, naturality of $\beta$ is $G(U_Ya)\beta_L=\beta_{L'}U_X(G^{\mathrm W}a)$; multiplying on the left by $q_{L'}$ and on the right by $q_L$ gives $q_{L'}G(U_Ya)=U_X(G^{\mathrm W}a)q_L$. Hence $\beta$ is a natural isomorphism without requiring a functor $L\mapsto H_L$.

proof.text:
The transpose equation from Step 2, followed by composition with $c_{G^{\mathrm W}L}$, is the asserted counit identity. For the unit, the inverse mate formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to $\beta$ and evaluated at $K$, reads
$$\epsilon_{U_YF^{\mathrm W}K}F(\beta_{F^{\mathrm W}K}U_X(\eta^{\mathrm W}_K))=c_K^{-1}.$$
Apply the ordinary adjunction's inverse transpose map $t\mapsto G(t)\eta_{U_XK}$ to this equality. Mutual inverseness of the Hom maps gives $\beta_{F^{\mathrm W}K}U_X(\eta^{\mathrm W}_K)=G(c_K^{-1})\eta_{U_XK}$. Composing with $G(c_K)$ proves the asserted unit identity.

proof.text: For any second representing triple $(H'_L,e'_L,d'_L)$ the same computation gives $e'_LU_X(h'_L)=\beta_L=e_LU_X(h_L)$, since Step 2 never used a triple. More explicitly $a_L=h'_Lh_L^{-1}:H_L\to H'_L$ satisfies $d'_LF^{\mathrm W}(a_L)=d_L$; injectivity of the second triple's representing bijection makes it the unique such map. The displayed equality gives $e'_LU_X(a_L)=e_L$. Thus even the expressions obtained from different representing objects agree canonically. Every cancellation above occurs in a stated Hom bijection or uses an explicit inverse, so neither fullness nor faithfulness of the forgetful functors is needed.

lean.statement: theorem forgetful_representingPair_rightMate (adjW : FW ⊣ GW) (adj : F ⊣ G) (c : FW ⋙ UY ≅ UX ⋙ F) (H : WY → WX) (e : ∀ L : WY, UX.obj (H L) ≅ G.obj (UY.obj L)) (d : ∀ L : WY, FW.obj (H L) ⟶ L) (hd : ∀ L : WY, UY.map (d L) = c.hom.app (H L) ≫ F.map (e L).hom ≫ adj.counit.app (UY.obj L)) (hbij : ∀ (L : WY) (K : WX), Function.Bijective (fun u : K ⟶ H L => FW.map u ≫ d L)) : IsIso (forgetfulRightMate adjW adj c) ∧ (∀ L : WY, ∃ h : GW.obj L ≅ H L, FW.map h.hom ≫ d L = adjW.counit.app L ∧ (∀ h' : GW.obj L ≅ H L, FW.map h'.hom ≫ d L = adjW.counit.app L → h' = h) ∧ (forgetfulRightMate adjW adj c).app L = UX.map h.hom ≫ (e L).hom) ∧ (∀ L : WY, (forgetfulRightMate adjW adj c).app L = adj.homEquiv (UX.obj (GW.obj L)) (UY.obj L) (c.inv.app (GW.obj L) ≫ UY.map (adjW.counit.app L))) ∧ (∀ L : WY, c.hom.app (GW.obj L) ≫ F.map ((forgetfulRightMate adjW adj c).app L) ≫ adj.counit.app (UY.obj L) = UY.map (adjW.counit.app L)) ∧ (∀ K : WX, UX.map (adjW.unit.app K) ≫ (forgetfulRightMate adjW adj c).app (FW.obj K) ≫ G.map (c.hom.app K) = adj.unit.app (UX.obj K)) ∧ (∀ (L : WY) (H' : WX) (e' : UX.obj H' ≅ G.obj (UY.obj L)) (d' : FW.obj H' ⟶ L), UY.map d' = c.hom.app H' ≫ F.map e'.hom ≫ adj.counit.app (UY.obj L) → (∀ K : WX, Function.Bijective (fun u : K ⟶ H' => FW.map u ≫ d')) → ∀ (h : GW.obj L ≅ H L) (h' : GW.obj L ≅ H'), FW.map h.hom ≫ d L = adjW.counit.app L → FW.map h'.hom ≫ d' = adjW.counit.app L → UX.map h.hom ≫ (e L).hom = UX.map h'.hom ≫ e'.hom)
